{{Short description|Ancient Japanese city halls}}
{{one source|date=January 2023}}
{{nihongo|'''Gunga'''|郡衙}} was the central government office of a county under the [[Ritsuryō|Ritsuryo system]] of ancient Japan. It was responsible for local control and administration, and was placed under the national government.<ref name="Bunka" /> Small administrative units analogous to [[counties]] were called {{Nihongo|gun|郡}}.<ref name="CHJ">{{cite book |author=Shively, Donald H. |title=Cambridge History of Japan vol. II (p.31f.) |author2=McCullough, William H. |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |year=1999}}</ref> The official in charge of a Gunga was known as a gunji, and the county was typically controlled by 2 to 8 appointed county governors. These governors were appointed by powerful local clans and were responsible for tasks such as tax collection.<ref name="日本国語大辞典防府市歴史用語集テシタル大辞泉世界大百科事典内言及-2023a">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,防府市歴史用語集,デジタル大辞泉,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,精選版 |title=郡衙(ぐんが)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%83%A1%E8%A1%99-162056 |access-date=2023-01-24 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref> The [[Niihari Gunga ruins]] are notable ruins of a Gunga.<ref name="Bunka">{{cite web |title=新治郡衙跡 |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138037 |accessdate=25 May 2020 |work=Cultural Heritage Online |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |language=Japanese}}</ref> [[Shida Gunga ruins]] is another such example.<ref>{{cite web |title=志太郡衙跡 |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/162871 |accessdate= |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |language=Japanese}}</ref>

The Ritsuryo system was enforced in the 640s, and in 703, the [[Taihō Code|Taiho Code]] was established which changed the council system to a county system. Remains of Gunga offices have been discovered in various locations, including Niihari County in [[Hitachi Province]], Nasu County in [[Shimotsuke Province]], and Tamana County in [[Higo Province]].<ref name="日本国語大辞典防府市歴史用語集テシタル大辞泉世界大百科事典内言及-2023a" />

The Gunga also had a [[kitchen]] to prepare food for the officials and visitors. The term Gunga is also known as Gunke or Kokuga. It is similar to a modern-day [[city hall]] and was responsible for controlling the county during the Ritsuryo era.<ref name="日本国語大辞典防府市歴史用語集テシタル大辞泉世界大百科事典内言及-2023a" />
